headline: Vertiv (+15%) and GE Vernova beat and raised on orders up over 100%, and SK Hynix sees memory shortage to 2030, so the bottleneck trade got hard earnings proof on the day before the Fed.
regime: Another bounce inside a drawdown, but this one has earnings behind it: the semis ETF rose 3.0% and neoclouds 7.1% on the day, yet the semis are still -7.0% on the month and neoclouds -21.2%. The 10-year is 4.99% and crude $101.76 (+9.9% on the month), so the discount rate is still punishing long-duration names ahead of the Fed decision. Five-day returns are mixed (grid -2.9%, hyperscalers -4.1%, ai_software +7.9%), so money is still rotating rather than piling back into the build-out. The suppliers with real orders (Vertiv, GE Vernova, SK Hynix) are being paid; the spenders (Meta -10.7% on five days) are not.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Vertiv Q3 sales +61%, organic orders over 100%, guidance raised on all metrics, stock +15% (cc8431617a49, d516dda2b5b5)
GE Vernova beat EBITDA ($1.9B vs $1.7B), orders soared, guidance raised and it is buying Trench Group (a2a65c739347, 7e7e3af5b2d5)
Baker Hughes won a 1.1 GW integrated power and cooling order from a US tech client; Constellation got a $5B DOE loan for nuclear uprates (83cc3d6476e8, 161d786e5438)
Against: Hubbell fell on a guidance-lifting beat and the segment is -2.9% on five days (c3d2c6c1edf3)
theses.change_note: +5: the two reports we were waiting on both showed orders running well ahead of sales; the Hubbell reaction shows that good news is not automatically paid for.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: SK Hynix profit +632% and it expects demand to exceed supply through 2030 (38284399fdfa, ff9825d0b553)
Celestica revenue +83% on networking and compute demand (0c3973789b59)
Lumentum is up 383% in a year with fiscal 2026 revenue +83% (8baa4641742e)
Against: Amazon told coders to rein in AI use as costs mount; OpenAI is reportedly buying Google chips, a hit to Nvidia's leverage (beb0b02d481d, d7893caf2c65)
theses.change_note: +4: a memory maker's own multi-year shortage call and another server beat add supply-tightness evidence; Amazon's cost curbs are the first sign of end-user budget limits.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Segment +7.1% on the day but still -21.2% on the month and +0.8% on five days, with CIFR -4.5% over five days (digest segments)
Meta's $25B stock sale drew five times the demand, so capital is available to the strongest borrowers, not the weakest (f2398ad178f4)
Yahoo feeds for CORZ, IREN, NBIS, CRWV and others failed today, so there is no fresh company news on them
theses.change_note: -4: the one-day bounce and strong demand for Meta's raise show funding is open for quality, but nothing here repairs neocloud balance sheets; the quality gate still drops most of them as cash-burners.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: SK Hynix says shortage lasts until 2030 and pledged $45B to shareholders; Micron, SanDisk and Western Digital rose in sympathy (38284399fdfa, a1df8b21dea8)
Segment is -19.8% on the month and Seagate fell 25% in a month despite record earnings and a raised outlook (71ae28d25374)
Against: the market is selling records, which is what a peak looks like (31f0ee31a52a)
theses.change_note: +6: management of the largest producer now says the shortage runs to 2030, while prices stay down about a fifth; the 'peak' pricing is the debate, not the demand.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Meta is -10.7% on five days and just raised $25B of equity (f2398ad178f4)
Amazon is cutting back coder AI use over budget overruns (beb0b02d481d)
Segment is -4.1% on five days while ai_software is +7.9%; Microsoft, Alphabet and the Fed report today (5656dc8596fe)
theses.change_note: +2: Amazon's cost curbs and Meta's equity raise reinforce the cash squeeze; Microsoft and Alphabet tonight are the real test.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: 10-year at 4.99%, crude $101.76 (+9.9% on the month) and the dollar firm ahead of the Fed (digest tape, c6d940de3e8c)
Semis ETF is -7.0% on the month despite +3.0% today; VIX 17.44, up 8.5% on the month
Data center equipment stocks fell a median 23% since Oct. 6 despite record backlogs (b929e7241255)
theses.change_note: Rates and oil have not moved enough either way, and the Fed decision is the next catalyst.

compute.note: +3.2% today but -7.6% on the month; OpenAI buying Google chips is a lever shift away from Nvidia.

foundry_equipment.note: -15.8% on the month and LRCX -8.6% over five days; demand is intact but the group is still being sold.

memory_storage.note: SK Hynix calls shortage through 2030 while the group is -19.8% on the month.

networking_optical.note: +7.0% today on the sold-out story but -12.2% on the month; chase nothing.

servers.note: Dell +8.8% and Celestica +83% sales, but CLS -7.7% on five days shows beats are not enough.

power_nuclear.note: Own producers with cash flow; Constellation's $5B DOE loan supports uprates.

grid_electrical.note: GE Vernova orders soar; Hubbell sold off on a beat, which helps entry prices.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv orders over 100% organic; the 15% jump costs some of the margin of safety.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -21.2% on the month; a one-day bounce does not fix the debt.

hyperscalers.note: Meta -10.7% on five days and Amazon capping AI spend; wait for Microsoft and Alphabet.

ai_software.note: +7.9% over five days is rotation (CRWD +17.9%), not a bottleneck play.

risks: A hawkish Fed with the 10-year at 4.99% and crude above $100 would extend multiple compression in crowded AI names.
Microsoft or Alphabet capex cuts tonight would hit the whole supplier chain despite strong supplier orders.
Amazon's AI cost curbs could spread to other end users and slow demand growth.
Neocloud credit stress could still reach GPU, power and cooling suppliers through cancelled orders.
Sell-the-news reactions (Hubbell, Seagate) show strong prints can still lose money.
watch: Fed decision today and the 10-year against 5%.
Microsoft and Alphabet capex and cloud growth after the close.
Quanta (Oct. 29) and MasTec results for grid build-out demand.
Whether Vertiv and GE Vernova hold their gains over the next two sessions.
Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO terms and any neocloud debt raises.
